minutes.headline: ZBA deferred the Pond View Commons fee waiver and traffic, starting peer-review consultant selection; no water/sewer decision.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued the 200-unit Pond View Commons 40B hearing, taking up application fees, traffic, and the board's authority to waive water and sewer district requirements. The board postponed the fee question, voted to start identifying peer-review consultants, and heard extensive public comment. Water and sewer authority was debated by both attorneys with no determination made; the hearing was continued to October 26.

decisions.decision: The fee waiver question was postponed while the board gathers actual fees from prior 40B projects and estimates its processing costs.
Staff will identify peer-review consultants and gather scopes, with funding deposited before work begins.
Peer-review selection (traffic, civil, fire) will be handled in public at the Oct 26 session after the first case.
Board will seek feedback from the water district and Sewer Commission and review the intermunicipal agreements before deciding on water and sewer waivers.
Hearing continued to October 26 (peer review at about 7:30 after first case), with November 9 as a possible next date.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued the Pond View Commons 40B hearing to October 26, with November 9 named as a possible next date.
The board voted by voice to table traffic until consultant estimates are gathered, have staff identify peer-review consultants, and require agreed funds deposited first.
The fee waiver question was postponed while the board gathers fees paid by prior 40B projects and estimates its own processing costs.
No decision was made on waiving water and sewer district requirements; the board will seek feedback from the water district and Sewer Commission and review the intermunicipal agreements.
Peer-review selection for traffic, civil and fire will be handled in public on October 26, after the first case.

why_it_matters: The fee the developer pays, and who funds the outside traffic, civil and fire reviews, decides how much of the cost of reviewing a 200-unit project falls on the developer rather than the town budget.

Whether the Zoning Board of Appeals can waive water and sewer district requirements is unresolved, and it bears on whether the project connects to systems that residents and town meeting have planned and paid for, and on the long-term pump and storage costs the water superintendent raised.

Feedback from the water district and Sewer Commission, and the board's review of the intermunicipal agreements, before any water or sewer waiver decision.
